script:
export const meta = {
  name: 'pilot-day-picker',
  description: 'Pick one Claude day and one Gemini day for the mining pilot',
  phases: [{ title: 'Pick' }],
}
phase('Pick')
const picks = await agent(`Read-only scout in /home/user/BookMinder. First read .coordination/diary-scout.md — the full reconnaissance of claude-dev-log-diary/ (inventory, per-file token estimates, format quirks, user-turn counts). You are authorized to sample inside claude-dev-log-diary/.

TASK: We will pilot a rationale-mining swarm on exactly TWO day-files before the full run: one Claude-agent day and one Gemini-CLI day (days 011-016 are Gemini). Pick the best candidates.

Criteria, priority order: (1) NO sharding — exclude day-020; prefer ~20–50k tokens; (2) overlap era (day-010..day-019) — story-card-era rationale is the target; (3) maximize density of USER corrective/interrogative turns (discipline enforcement, design pushback, style teaching — remember Gemini files box-wrap user prompts as \`│ >\`, so \`^> \` greps return 0 spuriously there); (4) days with known incidents/decisions beat quiet execution days.

Method: light sampling only — grep turn markers with counts, read a few small windows (~40-60 lines) at high-density spots to gauge corrective quality. NO bulk reads.

Return as final text (no file output): ONE Claude pick + ONE Gemini pick, each justified in 3-4 lines (size, era, expected yield, notable content sampled), plus one-line runner-ups. Max 18 lines total.`, { model: 'opus', effort: 'xhigh', label: 'day-picker' })
return picks
result:
**PILOT PICKS**

**Claude → `/home/user/BookMinder/claude-dev-log-diary/day-019.md`** (43k tok, 5383 lines, no shard, 2025-07-07)
- Best in-band corrective density of any Claude file: 92 user turns, 38 corrective/interrogative (~1 per 1.1k tokens); 22 story-card refs.
- Incident-rich, not execution: L470 `> W8. Stop. What's going on?` halts the agent mid-`sqlite3 UPDATE` on a fixture DB; two `/expert-council` retros where the user rejects the first output (`some AI slop adjacent first takes... ultrathink`); explicit revert order at L1247; L1344 designs the next session's prompt to avoid the repeat.
- Second half is a clean ATDD teaching arc: `We are practicing ATDD, we should be going outside-in`, `Remove the untested code... then follow the proper tdd_discipline`, `Where are we in the TDD cycle?` — exactly the `<tdd_discipline>` provenance the mine targets.

**Gemini → `/home/user/BookMinder/claude-dev-log-diary/day-016.md`** (51k tok, 7718 lines, no shard, 2025-07-04)
- Densest Gemini day that isn't day-011: 71 user turns, 28 corrective, and **75 story-card refs — the highest of any Gemini file**, so card-era rationale is on tape.
- Real incident + real teaching: L1390 `Wait!!! What did you \`rm\` last time?!?! Not my REALD DB, right??!?` (fixture-vs-real-DB path confusion, resolved over ~130 lines); style rule taught verbatim at L641 `we don't need the excessive comments, the code is self documetning`; commit-narrative doctrine at L4835 (`explain to me the prefix convention, "feat(docs)" seems strange`) plus staging/`git rm` correction and a revert order at L5041.
- Bonus for a pilot: it is one of only two files using the box-wrapped prompt form, so it exercises the hard parse path before the full run.

**FORMAT CORRECTION (blocks the swarm if uncarried):** the scout report's `│ >` regex is wrong and returns 0. Actual Gemini marker is `^│  > ` (**two** spaces), and it applies **only to day-015 and day-016**; day-011–014 use plain `^> ` like Claude files. Corrected turn counts: 011=77, 012=28, 013=40, 014=8, 015=51, 016=71.

**Runner-ups:** Claude `day-018.md` (60k, 158 turns/64 corrective — richest absolute yield, but over the size band); Gemini `day-011.md` (96k, holds the story-card birth, over band) or `day-012.md` (23k, has the `Why are you completely overwriting cli_spec?!? WTF!!!` incident but only 8 corrective turns).
summary: Pick one Claude day and one Gemini day for the mining pilot
